review_candidates.description: Independent Food Company is home to some of the region's most recognised hospitality concepts, including SALT, Somewhere, Parker's, Shalwa, Somewhere, and Public. We are a fast-growing organisation with an expanding portfolio of concepts, an active acquisition strategy, and ambitious plans for growth across new and existing markets. As we scale, the quality of our people remains central to everything we build. That is where you come in. Role Summary The Operations Director is responsible for the end-to-end operational performance of assigned brands, ensuring each brand delivers against its commercial, operational, people, and guest experience objectives. The role acts as the operational owner of the brand, translating its strategy and positioning into consistent restaurant-level execution. The Operations Director leads the Area Management and restaurant teams, owns brand performance, supports growth and new openings, and works cross-functionally to ensure the brand continues to evolve while maintaining strong operational standards. Key Responsibilities 1. Brand Operational Leadership Take full operational ownership of assigned brands and their restaurant portfolio. Translate brand strategy, positioning, and business objectives into operational priorities and execution plans. Ensure consistent execution of the brand experience across all locations. Establish clear priorities and operating rhythms for each assigned brand. Act as the primary operational point of accountability for brand performance. 2. Commercial & Financial Performance Own brand-level and restaurant-level sales, profitability, labor, food cost, and controllable expenses. Review brand and restaurant P&Ls and identify opportunities to improve performance. Develop action plans for underperforming locations and ensure timely execution. Drive initiatives to increase sales, productivity, efficiency, and profitability. Work closely with Finance on budgets, forecasts, targets, and performance reviews. 3. Restaurant Operations & Standards Ensure all restaurants consistently meet operational, food, service, cleanliness, and brand standards. Maintain strong field presence and regularly review restaurant performance and execution. Ensure operational issues are identified, escalated, and resolved quickly. Drive consistency across locations while addressing individual restaurant performance requirements. Continuously identify opportunities to simplify and improve restaurant operations. 4. Guest Experience Own the operational delivery of the intended guest experience for assigned brands. Monitor guest feedback, complaints, ratings, and key experience indicators. Identify recurring guest experience gaps and implement corrective actions. Ensure teams consistently deliver the required service and hospitality standards. Work with relevant departments to continuously elevate the overall brand experience. 5. Operations Team Leadership Lead and manage Senior Area Managers, Area Managers, and restaurant leadership teams. Establish clear KPIs, responsibilities, and performance expectations. Conduct structured performance reviews and coaching with the Area Management team. Build accountability and strong leadership capability across the brand. Identify high-potential talent and develop succession plans for key operational roles. 6. Manpower, Recruitment & Development Own operational manpower requirements and workforce planning for assigned brands. Work with HR and Recruitment to ensure vacancies are filled in line with business requirements. Participate in the selection of key operational and restaurant leadership positions. Monitor turnover, retention, vacancies, productivity, and manpower efficiency. Partner with L&D to ensure operational teams receive the required technical, service, and leadership training. 7. Brand Growth & New Openings Lead operational readiness for all new openings under assigned brands. Ensure manpower, training, equipment, systems, stock, SOPs, and operational requirements are ready before opening. Represent Operations throughout the development and pre-opening process. Coordinate with Projects, Design, Culinary, Marketing, HR, Supply Chain, IT, Finance, and other departments. Lead post-opening stabilization and ensure new restaurants achieve expected performance and standards. 8. Brand Development & Cross-Functional Collaboration Represent Operations in all discussions and initiatives relating to assigned brands. Work closely with Brand, Marketing, Culinary, Projects, Design, Supply Chain, QA/QC, Finance, HR, and other functions. Provide operational input into menu development, campaigns, pricing, promotions, design changes, and brand initiatives. Assess the operational impact and feasibility of proposed brand initiatives before implementation. Ensure approved initiatives are successfully implemented across the restaurant network. 9. Quality, SOPs & Compliance Ensure consistent implementation of brand SOPs, recipes, operational procedures, and company policies. Partner with QA/QC to maintain food safety, product quality, and compliance standards. Review operational and QA audits and ensure corrective actions are completed. Ensure compliance with all applicable municipality, food safety, health and safety, and regulatory requirements. Continuously review SOPs and processes to improve operational effectiveness. 10. Brand Performance Reporting Maintain clear visibility over the overall health and performance of assigned brands. Review sales, profitability, food cost, labor, guest experience, people, QA, and operational KPIs. Conduct structured weekly and monthly brand performance reviews. Present key performance updates, risks, challenges, and action plans to senior management. Ensure Area Managers maintain clear action plans and follow through on agreed priorities. Qualifications & Experience Bachelor’s degree in Hospitality, Business Administration, or a related field preferred. Significant experience in multi-unit restaurant operations with senior operational leadership responsibility. Proven ability to manage a brand or large restaurant portfolio through Area Management teams. Minimum industry experience 18-20 years Strong commercial understanding of restaurant P&Ls, sales, food cost, labor, and profitability. Experience with new restaurant openings and rapidly growing F&B brands. Strong leadership, analytical, communication, and cross-functional management capabilities. Ability to balance brand thinking with strong operational and commercial execution .

review_candidates.description: Manutentionnaire: manipule les colis dans le cadre d’une opération, comprenant la manutention manuelle, les activités de tri et l’inspection, et exécute toutes les tâches ou formalités administratives associées. FedEx a développé une philosophie qui place l’individu au premier plan, et que nous prenons très au sérieux. En tant qu’employeur, nous prônons l’égalité des chances professionnelles et pouvons nous targuer de disposer d’un personnel diversifié et inclusif auquel nous offrons des possibilités d’évolution. Notre société FedEx est l’une des plus grandes sociétés internationales de transport express et figure régulièrement parmi les 10 entreprises les plus admirées au monde dans le classement établi par le magazine Fortune. Chaque jour, FedEx propose à ses clients des solutions professionnelles et de transport, dans plus de 220 pays et territoires à travers le monde. Nous répondons aux besoins de ce réseau mondial grâce aux membres incroyables de l’équipe FedEx, qui ont pour tâche de faire de chaque mission confiée à FedEx une expérience hors du commun. Notre philosophie La philosophie People-Service-Profit (P-S-P) décrit parfaitement les principes qui régissent la moindre décision, politique ou activité de FedEx. FedEx prend soin de son personnel, qui lui offre en retour le service impeccable exigé par les clients, nous assurant ainsi la rentabilité nécessaire pour asseoir notre viabilité future. Le succès de la philosophie People-Service-Profit de notre société tient essentiellement au fait que nous bouclons la boucle, en réinjectant les bénéfices dans nos activités et en investissant dans notre personnel. Nous devons notre réussite au sein de notre secteur d’activité à nos employés. Au travers de notre philosophie P-S-P, nous avons mis en place un environnement de travail qui encourage les membres de l’équipe à faire preuve d’innovation en vue d’offrir un service de qualité optimale à nos clients. Nous veillons à leur bien-être et attachons beaucoup de prix à leurs contributions à l’entreprise. Notre culture Notre culture est importante pour de nombreuses raisons et nous faisons en sorte de l’incarner au travers de nos comportements, de nos actions et de nos activités aux quatre coins du monde. La culture et les valeurs de FedEx constituent la pierre angulaire du succès et de la croissance de notre société depuis qu’elle a vu le jour au début des années 1970. Même si d’autres sociétés copient nos systèmes, notre infrastructure et nos processus, notre culture nous rend unique et constitue bien souvent un élément différenciateur tandis que nous rivalisons avec la concurrence et nous développons sur le marché mondial actuel. Égalité, opportunités et diversité (EO&D) Chez FedEx, notre plus grand atout est notre personnel. Nous nous engageons à construire un environnement de travail diversifié, équitable et inclusif, et à offrir l’égalité des chances, l’équité et le respect à toutes les personnes, quelles qu’elles soient. Nous vous encourageons à postuler même si vous estimez que votre expérience ne correspond pas à tous les aspects de la description du poste, car vous pourriez être exactement la personne que nous recherchons pour ce poste ou pour une autre opportunité. Nous ne tolérons aucune forme de discrimination ou de harcèlement fondée sur la couleur, l’ethnicité, l’origine nationale, la religion, le sexe, l’âge, les informations génétiques, la citoyenneté, le handicap, la situation matrimoniale, la grossesse, l’orientation sexuelle, l’identité de genre, l’expression de genre ou toute autre caractéristique protégée par les lois et réglementations nationales et internationales. Nous mettons en place des aménagements raisonnables pour les membres de notre équipe et les tiers afin de garantir un accès équitable, l’inclusion et le respect de l’égalité pour toutes les caractéristiques protégées.

review_candidates.title: Investments Director
review_candidates.description: Position Summary The Investments Director is a key leadership role within the finance organization, responsible for leading the company’s investment strategy, portfolio management, capital allocation, and transaction execution. This role requires a seasoned financial leader who can identify high-yield investment opportunities, perform rigorous financial modeling and risk assessment, oversee mergers and acquisitions (M&A), and manage strategic partnerships and joint ventures to maximize long-term shareholder value. Key Responsibilities 1. Investment Strategy & Capital Allocation Partner with executive leadership to formulate and execute the company’s long-term investment strategy and capital allocation framework. Evaluate macroeconomic trends, industry dynamics, and market conditions to identify emerging investment opportunities, asset classes, or growth sectors. Design and implement robust portfolio management strategies to optimize risk-adjusted returns across existing and new investments. 2. Transaction Execution & M&A Lead the end-to-end deal lifecycle for mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, joint ventures, and strategic minority/majority stakes. Direct comprehensive financial, commercial, legal, and operational due diligence processes in coordination with internal teams and external advisors. Oversee enterprise valuation, advanced financial modeling, and scenario/sensitivity analyses for prospective transactions. Lead deal structuring, term sheet negotiations, and closing processes in alignment with corporate governance standards. 3. Portfolio Management & Value Creation Monitor the financial and operational performance of portfolio companies, subsidiaries, and strategic investments. Collaborate with portfolio company management teams to drive post-merger integration, synergy realization, and strategic value-creation initiatives. Prepare regular executive reporting, board presentations, and performance dashboards regarding portfolio health, returns, and key value drivers. 4. Risk Management & Compliance Establish and enforce rigorous risk assessment frameworks to evaluate market, liquidity, credit, and operational risks for all prospective and ongoing investments. Ensure full compliance with internal investment policies, local/international regulatory requirements, tax frameworks, and statutory reporting standards. Coordinate with legal and compliance teams to manage governance structures for joint ventures and special-purpose vehicles (SPVs). 5. Leadership & Team Collaboration Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing team of financial analysts, investment managers, and project specialists. Work cross-functionally with Corporate Finance, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), Treasury, and Legal teams to ensure alignment on liquidity, funding strategies, and cash flow planning. Cultivate and manage relationships with external stakeholders, including investment banks, private equity firms, venture capitalists, legal counsel, and financial auditors. Qualifications & Requirements Education: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field. An MBA, CFA, or professional designation (e.g., CPA, CA, CIMA) is strongly preferred. Experience: professional experience in corporate finance, investment banking, private equity, venture capital, or within the investment division of a major corporation. Demonstrated track record of successfully closing complex transactions (M&A, joint ventures, fundraisings) and managing large-scale investment portfolios. Technical Skills: Expert-level proficiency in financial modeling, valuation methodologies (DCF, LBO, comparable company analysis), and investment appraisal. Deep familiarity with ERP systems, financial reporting standards (IFRS/GAAP), and corporate tax/regulatory frameworks. Soft Skills: Exceptional strategic thinking, analytical prowess, and problem-solving capabilities. Outstanding negotiation, stakeholder management, and executive communication skills. Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams in a fast-paced, dynamic environment. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Accuracy of financial valuations and due diligence findings. Successful execution and integration of strategic M&A or investment projects. Risk-adjusted financial returns (IRR, ROI) on the investment portfolio. Effectiveness of portfolio monitoring, cost control, and value-creation initiatives. Leadership effectiveness and team development.
